question: In meta-harness, what happens end to end when an agent requests the bash tool: how is the command classified and approved, how do foreground and background commands execute and terminate, and how does the result get back into the next model turn?

requiredFacts.description: The agent loop resolves a phase-local tool first, refuses a global tool omitted from allowedGlobalTools even if the model calls it, otherwise dispatches through executeTool, and converts thrown or unknown-tool failures into error results.

bash trims the raw command, interprets a trailing ampersand as background mode and strips it, rejects an empty remainder, and before safety classification refuses direct scip-query CLI use in favor of the dedicated scip tool.
Classification always blocks fork-bomb patterns, sudo or doas command words, and recursive forced deletion of literal system roots; session auto-approve does not bypass these hard blocks.

Confirmation is required for any rm -rf, force push, hard reset, git clean -f, recursive chmod, download piped to a shell, write-style targets outside the project, and redirects outside it; relative paths are resolved from the project root and leading home paths expand. Auto-approve bypasses this tier, while missing or denied confirmation prevents execution.

A background command is handed to the singleton ProcessManager, which spawns sh -c in the project root, writes combined output to .meta-harness/logs while retaining a bounded recent buffer, tracks running/exited/killed/error state, and returns its id, log path, and process_output/kill_process instructions immediately.

A foreground command spawns sh -c in the project root with ignored stdin and piped output; timeout is clamped from 1,000 to 600,000 ms with a 60,000 ms default, each collected stream is capped at 10 MiB, user abort is rethrown, and timeout or buffer overflow aborts the child but becomes a rendered result.

Foreground output is assembled from the command, stdout, labeled stderr, exit/signal/error/timeout details and truncated to 16,000 bytes; the loop reports the result callback, creates a tool_result preserving tool_use_id, content and isError, appends all results as a user message, and starts the next chat round unless a successful terminal tool ended the phase or cancellation intervened.

answerIncludesAny: yolo mode allows sudo and system-root deletion
the bash call waits for a background process to exit
background output is returned only after the child finishes
non-interactive mode automatically runs confirm-tier commands
